newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen mixed.

text.p: Fresh wedding season buying in India and subdued demand for jewellery ahead of general elections in Pakistan are expected to keep gold prices mixed in the Indian sub-continent, dealers said on Monday.
On the Bombay bullion market, gold prices rose 20 rupees per 10 grammes to 4,900 rupees in the week to Monday and dealers said they expected the trend to stay firm in the next few days.
Initially the market turned weak after a fresh drop in world prices but recovered on renewed buying, dealers said.
"I expect fresh physical buying during the second round of wedding season which has just begun and will last up to May," said leading jeweller Babubhai Jain.
A month-long inauspicious period during which Hindus desisted from buying gold had also ended by mid-January, Jain said.
Dealers said arrivals of imported gold from Dubai, the Gulf re-export centre which feeds the demand for gold in the Indian sub-continent, had also been low.
"Overall market sentiment is firm. Prices are likely to rise further because of the limited supplies of gold," Jain said.
In Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi, gold prices fell 56 rupees per 10 grammes and dealers said they expected the bullion trend to remain mixed in the next few days.
Dealers said demand for jewellery was expected to remain subdued ahead of the February 3 general elections.
"Demand for jewellery has fallen before the elections," one dealer said. He did not elaborate.
Traders in Dubai said demand was gaining strength in the second week of Ramadan ahead of Eid al-Fitr holidays - a traditionally buoyant time for sales.
"The prices are good for the customers at the moment. Lower prices have boosted demand and we don't expect them to climb very much this week," said one trader.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
